access: Necessary primary-source text located by search and confirmed with direct HTTP plus a standard HTML text parser. No browser, page image, screenshot or visual retrieval.
bindingScope: This file binds short excerpts and review observations. primary-text-bindings.json records the actually received response-byte hashes and necessary-window hashes; it does not claim unseen full-page visual review.

sources.title: Realization of the candela
shortExcerpts: spectral responsivity of the human visual system
normalized to unity at its peak, 555 nm
observations: The CIE visual-response function is a defined spectral response, not an individual observer's informal brightness estimate.
The retrieved equation relates photometric values to spectral radiometric values using a weighted wavelength integral and a luminous efficacy factor.
The photopic function has its peak at 555 nm; a qualified statement that green light is relatively well detected under photopic conditions is consistent with this.
The source distinguishes the calibration frequency and luminous efficacy from arbitrary emitter selection.

sources.title: Point source, CIE S 017:2020 e-ILV
shortExcerpts: A point source that emits uniformly in all directions
observations: A source can be treated as point-like when its dimensions are negligible compared with its distance from the receiving surface.
Uniform or isotropic point source is a further property, not a necessary consequence of negligible source size.

sources.title: Luminous intensity of a source in a given direction
observations: The directional intensity definition is differential: luminous flux in a directional solid-angle element divided by that element.
Its stated unit is cd = lm per sr.
The finite-region average and constant-emission conditions below are reviewer derivations from this definition, not quotations from the candidate.

sources.title: Steradian
shortExcerpts: cuts off an area of the surface of the sphere
observations: The unit is defined using a sphere centered at the angle's vertex and a surface area equal to a square whose side is the sphere radius.
Therefore the area in S/R² must be the intercepted spherical area, not an arbitrary flat target area.

sources.title: Recommendation 1 of the 69th CIPM, 1980
observations: The recommendation explicitly describes solid angle as an area divided by a squared length and interprets steradian as a dimensionless derived unit.
Used only for the dimensional interpretation, not as a claim that the historical supplementary-unit classification remains current.

sources.title: Lumen
observations: Luminous flux uses lumen, not watt; the CIE entry ties the lumen to a specified monochromatic radiant flux.
Together with the CIE intensity unit relation, this supports 1 lm = 1 cd sr for constant intensity over the selected solid angle.

independentDerivations.reasoning: Photopic luminous flux is obtained by weighting spectral radiant flux by the defined visual response and the luminous-efficacy factor. Bare radiant power in watts is not thereby identical to luminous flux in lumens. The lesson's evaluated-power wording is interpreted with its explicit visual weighting and lumen unit, not as a numerical equality of W and lm.

Integrating the directional definition gives Φ_A = integral_A I(ω)dΩ. Thus Φ_A/Ω_A is the angular average for Ω_A > 0, and equals the directional intensity throughout A only if intensity is constant on that region.

All directions cover 4π sr. With direction-independent intensity, integrating yields Φ_total = 4π I; without this assumption Φ_total/(4π) is only a full-sphere angular mean. Point-like geometry alone does not justify uniform emission.

For a fixed ray region and a sphere of positive radius centered at the vertex, dilation scales the intercepted area by R². Hence S/R² is radius-independent; the boundary need not be circular. For the entire sphere, S = 4πR².

historyScope: Block18 is audited as a description of the actual Chinese source footnote and its owner, not as a universal equivalence of every historical candle standard with the modern candela.
